plan.headline: Lotus Tile & Stone: $6,780 in IEEPA tariff refunds must be claimed today (Oct 24, 2026), and $73,460 in total IEEPA duties were paid across 13 entries.

steps.title: Today: claim entry HP7-0414106-2 in CAPE
steps.detail: CAPE is the CBP online tool for claiming IEEPA tariff refunds. This entry ($6,780) appears eligible, but its deadline is today, so call or email your broker right away to file it.

steps.title: Claim entry HP7-0414533-5 in CAPE
steps.detail: This entry ($13,230) appears eligible for CAPE. Together with the entry above, that's $20,010 ready to claim, and this one is due Nov 16, 2026.

steps.title: File a protest for entry HP7-0413540-6
steps.detail: This entry ($3,640) was finalized too long ago for CAPE, so CAPE will reject it. A protest is a formal written challenge filed with CBP, and it is still allowed until Nov 22, 2026.

steps.title: Fix entry HP7-0414879-0, then claim it in CAPE
steps.detail: A goods value was reported on a Chapter 99 line, and CAPE rejects the entry until your broker moves it to the Chapter 1-97 line. This entry ($4,460) should be fixed and filed by Nov 30, 2026.

steps.title: File a protest for entry HP7-0413822-4
steps.detail: CAPE will reject this entry ($15,840) because it was finalized too long ago, but it appears eligible for a protest until Dec 12, 2026.

steps.title: File a protest for entry HP7-0414117-9
steps.detail: This entry ($3,750) also needs a protest rather than CAPE, and the protest window runs until Jan 31, 2027. Your three protest entries total $23,230.

steps.title: Ask your broker about the surety-paid entry
steps.detail: CBP says not to file a CAPE claim when a surety (the bond company) paid the IEEPA duties. This entry ($3,975) needs a conversation with your broker about the right route.

steps.title: Check three entries by hand
steps.detail: The app couldn't verify a key fact (the liquidation date or the IEEPA duty amount) for these entries, so it didn't guess. Ask your broker to confirm the details from the official records.

steps.title: Wait on the court for two finalized entries
steps.detail: These entries ($6,985 total) were finalized more than 180 days ago with no protest. A court has certified a group of importers who haven't sued, but there is no refund order yet, and the group may not cover goods from Brazil or India. For a large balance, ask a customs attorney about filing your own suit.

steps.title: No action needed on one entry
steps.detail: No IEEPA duty was paid on this entry, so there is nothing to refund. Section 301 and 232 duties are not part of this refund.

plan.broker_email_subject: URGENT: IEEPA refund filings for Lotus Tile & Stone LLC (one due today, Oct 24, 2026)
plan.broker_email_body:
Hello,

I'm reviewing our IEEPA tariff refund options, and several entries appear eligible. Please confirm the details and let me know what you need from me. One entry has a deadline today.

1. CAPE filing, please file as soon as possible:
- HP7-0414106-2 ($6,780). The deadline is today, Oct 24, 2026.
- HP7-0414533-5 ($13,230). The deadline is Nov 16, 2026.

2. Fix, then CAPE:
- HP7-0414879-0 ($4,460). A goods value appears to be on a Chapter 99 line, which CAPE rejects. Can you correct it so the value sits on the Chapter 1-97 line, then file by Nov 30, 2026?

3. Protests, since these entries appear to be too old for CAPE:
- HP7-0413540-6 ($3,640), due Nov 22, 2026
- HP7-0413822-4 ($15,840), due Dec 12, 2026
- HP7-0414117-9 ($3,750), due Jan 31, 2027

4. Surety-paid entry:
- HP7-0416018-4 ($3,975). CBP says not to file CAPE for entries where a surety paid the IEEPA duties. What is the right route for this one?

5. Please verify these entries, because I couldn't confirm the liquidation date or IEEPA duty amount:
- HP7-0415250-8
- HP7-0415702-7
- HP7-0416475-1

6. For your awareness, HP7-0412207-3 and HP7-0412988-1 were finalized more than 180 days ago with no protest. I understand they are waiting on the court's class action and have no refund order yet. Please tell me if you see any other option.

Please confirm which of these you can file and by when.

Thank you,
Lotus Tile & Stone LLC

checker.summary: I checked 12 of the 13 extracted entries against the 7501s and the broker statement. They match on liquidation status and date, Chapter 99 lines, and IEEPA totals. Section 301 lines (9903.88.15 and 9903.88.03) are correctly kept out of the IEEPA totals. The surety-paid flag on HP7-0416018-4 is supported by the statement note. The only problem is HP7-0416475-1: it has no 7501, so its 3,180 IEEPA figure and its missing Chapter 99 lines cannot be verified. The statement and the 7501 pages also repeat HP7-0415702-7 and HP7-0415250-8 with look-alike characters in the filer code. These are duplicates, not new entries, and the extraction handled them correctly.

reader_notes: Part 1 of 3 covers only 1_cbp7501_entry_summaries.pdf, pages 1-10. These pages show 10 entries, all type 01, filed by Harbor Point Customs Brokers (HP7). The importer on every page is Lotus Tile & Stone LLC, IOR 84-2917365-00.
None of these pages says anything about liquidation, so every entry is marked 'unknown'. The liquidation date is left empty.

None of these pages mentions surety payment, protests, drawback, reconciliation, AD/CVD, a broker IEEPA amount, or a Court of International Trade case. Those fields are left false or empty. Parts 2 and 3 may add these facts for the same entries.
Page 8 (HP7-0414879-0) prints an entered value of 22,300.00 on the 9903.02.69 row. It is copied as printed. On every other page, the Chapter 99 rows show no entered value, so those are left empty.
Page 9 (HP7-0415250-8) shows 'Free' for 6910.10.0030, recorded as rate 0.

Chapter 99 rows are copied exactly as printed, including 9903.88.15 and 9903.88.03 (pages 4 and 7). No row was labeled as IEEPA, Section 301 or Section 232 here; telling them apart is left to whoever reviews the data.
Each page's duty total matches the sum of its line duties.
Every page says it is a synthetic sample, not a real filing.

Page 13 entry number is printed as 'НР7-0415702-7', where both 'Н' and 'Р' are Cyrillic letters, not Latin H and P. Page 14 entry number is printed as 'HР7-0415250-8', with a Latin 'H' and a Cyrillic 'Р'. I copied both exactly as printed. They probably mean filer code HP7 (HP7-0415702-7 and HP7-0415250-8), but check this before matching them against other parts of the paperwork.

None of these pages say anything about liquidation, so all four entries are 'unknown'. No document here mentions surety payment, protests, drawback, reconciliation or AD/CVD, so those flags are false.
These pages include no broker statement, report or email, so ieepa_duty_statement is null for every entry. No document here says the importer is a CIT plaintiff.
Chapter 99 rows show no entered value, so entered_value is null for them. I copied them exactly as printed: 9903.02.20, 9903.88.15, 9903.02.69, 9903.01.24 and 9903.01.25.

Only one document was provided in this part: 2_broker_duty_statement.pdf. It is a summary statement with no 7501 line detail, so 'lines' is empty for every entry. HTS and Chapter 99 rows need to come from the 7501 pages in the other parts.

The last two rows of the statement repeat HP7-0415702-7 and HP7-0415250-8. Those repeated entry numbers are printed with Cyrillic letters that look like Latin ones ('НР7' and 'HР7'). Every other value matches the earlier rows, so I merged them into the normal HP7 entries and kept the Cyrillic text exactly as printed in the evidence. Check whether these rows are copy errors or something else.

The note 'Duties incl. IEEPA paid by surety after missed ACH; surety claim open' is printed right under the HP7-0416018-4 row. I took it to apply to that entry and set surety_paid_ieepa = true. Because the statement doesn't say which entry it applies to, please confirm.
The note '7501 copy not yet sent to client' is printed right under the HP7-0416475-1 row. It is not a flag; it is recorded here for reference.
Liquidation status 'Open' on the statement was recorded as unliquidated. The statement says liquidation dates are as posted in ACE.
IEEPA amounts are copied from the statement's 'IEEPA (9903.01/.02)' column. HP7-0411873-2 shows 0.00, recorded as 0.
The statement does not mention a CIT case, a protest, drawback, reconciliation or AD/CVD.
